--- title: "LFP Compression: Region-Decoding Validation" description: "Does lossy LFP compression degrade brain-region classification? A held-out XGBoost Cosmos-region decoder trained on LF-only features across the full 1099-PID ephys-atlas cohort, compared across compression tiers and ADC-saturation handling." date: "2026-09-05" author: "Olivier Winter" categories: [electrophysiology, LFP, compression, Neuropixels, decoding, region-classification] --- ## Overview [Decoding-aware tuning](compression_tuning.qmd) validated compression against wheel/choice/feedback behavioural decoding on 11 benchmark recordings. This page runs a second, independent functional check — **brain-region classification** — at full cohort scale (1099 PIDs, not 11), to see whether the same compression tiers hold up for an entirely different downstream task and a ~100× larger, more heterogeneous sample. **Bottom line:** the ranking matches the wheel/choice/feedback validation exactly — uncompressed > mild > default > aggressive — and the gaps are large enough to be functionally meaningful, not noise: compression cost is real and monotonic in both validations, on two unrelated decode targets, measured two different ways (behavioural regression/classification on 11 recordings vs. brain-region classification on 1099). ## Method Per-recording LF-band-power and CSD features (raw_lf + raw_lf_csd feature families, 33 columns, `ephysatlas.features.voltage_features_set`) are computed identically for every LFP source from ~8 snippets/PID (8.79 s windows, 600 s spacing, matching the canonical ephys-atlas snippet grid), aggregated into one channel-level table, then classified with the canonical ephys-atlas XGBoost pipeline (5-fold **PID-grouped** CV, Cosmos-level labels, `VINTAGE = "2026-08_lfp-decoders"`). | LFP source | Read from | Notes | |---|---|---| | `uncompressed` | `lf_resampled_car_cadzow.npy` (Cadzow checkpoint, pre-SVD/WP) | reference — already on the compute cluster | | `mild` | `lf_compressed_mild_all.h5` | lfpack SVD+WP ε=100, α=14 | | `default` | `lf_compressed_all.h5` | lfpack SVD+WP ε=150, α=28 | | `aggressive` | `lf_compressed_aggressive_all.h5` | lfpack SVD+WP ε=450, α=96 | Two snippet-selection modes are compared per source (except `mild`, run only at full-cohort scale for `all` — see [Recap](#recap)): naive (`all`) vs. **saturation-avoided**, which drops snippets overlapping an ADC-saturated interval. This isolates the saturation question from the compression question directly, on the same cohort. Cohort: every histology-resolved insertion in `ibl_neuropixel_brainwide_01` (the ephys-atlas cohort — a strict superset of the curated ~700-PID BWM behavioural cohort), **1099 PIDs, 407616 channels** per source/mode combination. ## Does compression hurt region decoding? ::: {#50884137 .cell execution_count=1} ::: {.cell-output .cell-output-display execution_count=1} ```{=html}
lfp_source snippet_mode accuracy n_pids n_channels
0 uncompressed all 0.468500 1099 407616
1 uncompressed saturation-avoided 0.470953 1099 407616
2 mild all 0.434706 1099 407616
3 default all 0.420096 1099 407616
4 default saturation-avoided 0.416753 1099 407616
5 aggressive all 0.389008 1099 407616
6 aggressive saturation-avoided 0.391597 1099 407616
``` ::: ::: ![Impact of LFP compression tier on region decoding — mean accuracy (Cosmos, held-out) across 1099 PIDs, snippet_mode="all". Same ranking as the wheel/choice/feedback validation.](figures/2026-09-05_lfp-decoders_compression-impact.png){.lightbox} Compression clearly costs region-decoding accuracy, and the cost is monotonic with compression aggressiveness: uncompressed (0.468) > mild (0.435, −3.3pp) > default (0.420, −4.8pp) > aggressive (0.389, −7.9pp vs. uncompressed). This mirrors the wheel/choice/feedback validation's ranking exactly, on a completely different task, decoder, and cohort scale — strong evidence that the compression-tier ordering is a real property of the codec, not an artefact of one validation's specific method. ## Does avoiding saturated snippets help? ![Impact of ADC saturation avoidance on region decoding — bars: mean ± SD across 5 folds; dots: individual folds. Restricted to the three sources with both snippet modes (`mild` is `all`-only, see Recap).](figures/2026-09-05_lfp-decoders_saturation-impact.png){.lightbox} Small and inconsistent in direction: default drops slightly avoiding saturation (−0.3pp), aggressive and uncompressed both gain slightly (+0.3pp, +0.2pp) — all differences are within the fold-to-fold spread seen within a single combo's own 5 folds. Avoiding ADC-saturated snippets does not meaningfully change region-decoding accuracy at this snippet-selection scale — a separate axis from the compression-tier effect above, and not something saturation handling needs to trade off against. ## Recap {#recap} ![Full numeric recap: accuracy mean/SD/min/max across folds, sample sizes, per source × snippet mode.](figures/2026-09-05_lfp-decoders_recap-table.png){.lightbox} `mild` was added to this validation after the wheel/choice/feedback grid had already identified ε=100/α=14 as the best-fidelity operating point worth naming and shipping (see [Decoding-aware tuning](compression_tuning.qmd#recommendation)) — run only at `snippet_mode="all"` full-cohort scale, not `saturation-avoided`, since the saturation question was already answered by the other three sources and doesn't need re-litigating per tier. ## Code Pipeline: `sdsc-slurms/2026-08_lfp-decoders/` — `extract.py` (per-PID/per-snippet LF+CSD feature extraction, joblib-parallel), `aggregate.py` (thin wrapper around `ephysatlas.aggregation.produce_output_dataframes`), `train_classifier.py` (5-fold PID-grouped XGBoost), `report.py` (this page's table + figures, run locally after rsyncing `accuracy.json` back from the cluster). Region annotations (`atlas_id`/`acronym`/`x`/`y`/`z`) come embedded in each lfpack archive via `attach_ibl_metadata.py` (`sdsc-slurms/2026-06-lfpack/`).
